barriers.description: The original interface was created by an experienced programming team that lacked usability training, producing design decisions not grounded in usability practice.
barriers.justification: Designers' lack of usability knowledge hindered their ability to produce user-centered design solutions and required the HCD team to expend effort correcting foundational interface choices, affecting specification of requirements and iterative design work.
barriers.reference_excerpt: This interface was designed by a skilled, experienced programming team, though untrained in usability.

barriers.description: Heterogeneous user perspectives and split questionnaire ratings produced ambiguous feedback that demanded additional analysis to interpret.
barriers.justification: Ambiguous and split user feedback increased the analytic burden on designers, impeding timely integration of feedback and iteration and complicating the specification of clear user requirements and priorities.
barriers.reference_excerpt: each from different agencies with somewhat differing user cultures; e.g., some involved the use of more students than others. Split ratings often indicate problem areas, but require more analysis of user comments than more consistent ratings.
